name: semble-92184916-blind30-454edc85-ots
instr:
# Repairing a semantic code-retrieval toolkit without a test suite

Someone points this tool at a directory or at a repository address, has the source text gathered and cut into pieces, and then asks it questions in plain language from a terminal or through the small server an assistant talks to. Every stage of that now misbehaves somewhere. The repository has received 30 separate undocumented edits.

Gathering material out of a directory goes wrong at the very first step: each resulting entry has its recorded location and its text interchanged, so no entry names a path that actually exists on disk, cloning a repository and building from it produces nothing that mentions what it contains, and asking for documentation prose alongside code no longer changes which suffixes show up in answers. Even when the language of a source is known, its text is cut without regard for that structure and falls back to plain line-by-line splitting. A pathologically deep nested expression that used to report hitting the recursion limit exactly once now reports it a different number of times, and cutting a short source against a tight size budget gives back pieces that overlap or go backwards, a later one beginning before the previous one ended, with the first no longer starting at offset zero. Merging tiny neighbouring lines is off as well: six two-character lines against a ten-character budget should come out as one group of five plus a remainder, and both the count and the offsets are wrong.
